question: Why does action appear so varied if it is essentially knowledge?
premises: Action is essentially of the nature of knowledge.
Within itself, action takes on a grosser form.
A grosser form allows manifold variation to appear.
inference: Therefore the diversity seen in action does not contradict its identity with knowledge.
plain_english: Action is in essence knowledge, but it takes on a grosser form. That is why such great variety is seen in it.
